macro_context.market_sentiment: Cautiously recovering — S&P 500 +0.55%, Nasdaq +0.70% on May 5 after a May 4 selloff. Markets are balancing a strong April earnings season against elevated oil prices (WTI ~$104/bbl, Brent ~$112.90) driven by the escalating U.S.-Iran military conflict threatening the Strait of Hormuz.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held benchmark rate at 3.5%–3.75% on April 29 (third consecutive hold), citing elevated inflation from energy prices and Middle East uncertainty. Most dissents since October 1992 (4 total). Market pricing forecasts one rate cut in late 2026 at best, with further cuts pushed to 2027.
macro_context.geopolitical: U.S.-Iran military conflict is the dominant risk: UAE intercepting Iranian missiles, U.S. defending Strait of Hormuz access. Oil supply shock is stoking inflation. Secondary risks: U.S. intervention in Venezuela (Maduro captured), NATO tensions around Greenland, ongoing U.S.-China trade/tech friction, and U.S. midterm election uncertainty.

web_context.competitor_activity: OpenAI's ChatGPT still holds dominant AI assistant market share but Google Gemini grew to ~13% share with massive distribution advantage. Google Gemini 3 appears to be outcompeting Apple's AI products (AAPL down 5% YTD). Google launched Ironwood custom AI chip, a potential threat to Nvidia in the AI accelerator market. Microsoft Azure Cloud growing but Google Cloud's +63% YoY growth rate is outpacing. Amazon launched a competing supply chain service (primarily targeting UPS/logistics), an indirect signal of increasing AI-native competition in enterprise services. OpenAI rumored to be developing an AI-optimized smartphone, but analysts believe Google would ultimately benefit from its full-stack AI position.
